title: Base-Editing Gene Therapy Successfully Targets Inherited Disorder | Inside Precision Medicine
summary:
Gene therapy has successfully treated a patient with alpha-1 antitrypsin (ATT) deficiency, according to the first report of its kind.

The Phase I/Ia clinical trial findings, in the Journal of Hepatology, offer an unprecedented insight into the safety and efficacy of in vivo base editing for the inherited condition, which can affect the liver and lungs.

They also suggest the technique could be used to treat different rare genetic variants and possibly even infectious diseases.

summary:

Lung function was also preserved among patients receiving efzofitimod, which was generally well tolerated.

title: Mayo Clinic reports early results from personalised gene-targeted ALS therapy | ACNR
summary:
Researchers at Mayo Clinic have reported encouraging early findings from an experimental treatment developed for a patient with a rare genetic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The single-patient study, published in the journal Med, explores how therapies designed to address specific disease-causing mutations could advance precision medicine for people with rare neurological disorders.

The treatment targets a mutation in the CHCHD10 gene, which is associated with a rare form of ALS.
